session_focus.summary: Built the TODOS.md <-> drift/retro sync loop end to end: check-todo-sync.js Stop hook (flags unsynced drift memory + retro JSON files against TODOS.md's last Log date), find-session.ps1 (greps session transcripts by keyword so a VSCode-tab-didn't-reopen doesn't mean the work is unfindable). Used the new hook live: triaged 3 pending retro files, closed the loop on trm-vault commit-per-run (promoted from memory-only to tracked Process rule), opened 2 real gaps (cic-ingestion tsx/tsconfig blind spot, trm-vault has no remote). Caught a live schema-gate failure on 3 retro JSONs (missing insertions_filtered/filter_note etc) rather than hand-faking them to pass - logged as its own backlog item instead.
incidents: 3 retro JSON files (2026-07-29-1, 2026-07-29-2, 2026-07-30-1) failed the canonical v1.0 retro schema gate at commit time - missing insertions_filtered/deletions_filtered/net_loc_filtered/filter_note (and more on 2 of them). Not hand-patched; left untracked and logged as an open backlog item pending a generator fix.

bulk_sync_commit 4f66345 (400 research-data/ file touches, dated 07-26) is still inside this window and remains the dominant hotspot signal - third retro in a row flagging the same commit's distortion.
Backlog open-count rose 6 -> 10 this period, but all 3 new items are real finds from building the sync tooling itself (schema drift, tsx/tsconfig gap, trm-vault remote gap), not accumulated neglect.
process_learnings: A sync hook is only as good as what it's allowed to silently fix - the retro-schema failure was the right kind of catch: the hook blocked a fake-passing commit instead of a human having to notice missing fields by hand.

Session-transcript search (find-session.ps1) turns 'my VSCode tab didn't reopen' from a data-loss scare into a one-command lookup - transcripts already persist independent of UI state, the gap was discoverability, not durability.
